newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end mostly lower.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended mostly lower on Tuesday as profit-taking especially in distant months gathered force on signs of a rebound in the yen, traders said.
The spot January contract was the only contract that rose.
Prices ranged from 210 yen per tonne lower to 170 yen higher, with the benchmark November 1997 contract falling 160 yen to 13,890 yen. Daily volume was 44,452 lots.
The market started the day on a mixed tone, with nearby months firmer, backed by the higher Chicago market, while distant months were pressured by constant technical selling, the traders said.
One trader said market players basically could not find any clear direction, and expected the benchmark November contract to move between 13,000 yen and 14,200 yen in the near-term.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.74 per bushel at 0834 GMT, against $2.74-3/4 at Monday's close.
The spot January contract of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was being traded at $7.07 per bushel at 0834 GMT, against $7.08 at Monday's close.
